issue_context.title: Custom DataUpdateCoordinator is not destructed on reload, disable or removal of integration
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Root issue: We have some issues with sessions not being closed when the HomeWizard integration is reloaded, disabled or removed. This causes some issues with the minimal resources of the device as it has a limited number of available memory and sessions.

I've isolated one of the issues to the coordinator not being destructed, keeping internal references active.

How to reproduce:
1. Add something like this to _a_ custom DeviceUpdateCoordinator, like the one from HomeWizard:
```python
def __del__(self):
        print("__del__ from DeviceUpdateCoordinator")
```
2. Reload the integration, see that `__del__ from DeviceUpdateCoordinator` _is not_ printend
3. Stop Home Assistant, Now it prints `__del__ from DeviceUpdateCoordinator` twice.

It seems that this has nothing to do with the API library itself, as it also triggers with the structure below. Maybe I do something wrong during init.

```python
class Api:
    """Some API"""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        LOGGER.warning("Api __init__")

    def __del__(self):
        print("Api __del__")


class HWEnergyDeviceUpdateCoordinator(DataUpdateCoordinator[None]):
    """Gather data for the energy device."""

    def __init__(self, hass, api: Api) -> None:
        """Initialize update coordinator."""
        super().__init__(hass, LOGGER, name=DOMAIN, update_interval=UPDATE_INTERVAL)
        LOGGER.warning("__init__ HWEnergyDeviceUpdateCoordinator")

        self.api = api

    def __del__(self):
        print("__del__ from HWEnergyDeviceUpdateCoordinator")

    async def _async_update_data(self) -> None:
        """Fetch all device and sensor data from api."""

        LOGGER.warning("Updating")
        await sleep(1)
        LOGGER.warning("Done")
```

Full PoC can be found here, where all implementation stuff is removed: https://github.com/DCSBL/home-assistant-core/blob/b7f21c0f67ec34647e6c59901677cbe26621757d/homeassistant/components/homewizard/

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2025.3.0.dev0 (development branch at cce6c73

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

Not sure

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/e24564147d302df8c20289136deb93813dc5212c/homeassistant/helpers/debounce.py#L33

It seems that `Debouncer_function` in Debouncer keeping a reference to the `DataUpdateCoordinator` and vice-verca, keeping the coordinator active. 

But the fact that this code is between 3 and 5 years old is worrying me (as in; I can't believe this is a bug, it must be something that I just don't understand)

Would it help if you release the reference to the function in the debouncer `async_shutdown` method?
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/f9cc3361e34b5174e66443b10000f36d905ffde6/homeassistant/helpers/debounce.py#L145-L146

Like this:
```python
    @callback
    def async_shutdown(self) -> None:
        """Cancel any scheduled call, and prevent new runs."""
        self._shutdown_requested = True
        self.async_cancel()
        self._function = None
```

It does, _sometimes_...

But when I also add `self._job = None` the Coordinator is destructed reliably.

```python
@callback
    def async_shutdown(self) -> None:
        """Cancel any scheduled call, and prevent new runs."""
        self._shutdown_requested = True
        self.async_cancel()
        self._function = None
        self._job = None
```
